Hans.q: A huge man in a butcher's apron and an iron pig mask, dragging a sledgehammer. He is the killer of the first film in Series 1 and the one who teaches you the game.
Hans.j: No special rules: he attacks, that's it. He starts with 12 health and Horror 4, and before the Finale his phase is simple: pick a target and attack.

Dr. Fright.q: A therapist with rotting skin and milky eyes who kills inside dreams. Whatever he does to you in there, you take with you when you wake up.
Dr. Fright.j: Starts with 9 health and Horror 4. He plays with the dream state: part of the danger is not being able to tell where you are.

Geppetto.q: A tall, pale ringmaster with a top hat and an ear-to-ear grin. He turns people into living puppets and adds them to his family.
Geppetto.j: 9 health and Horror 4. Every phase he spawns a puppet before moving, so the board fills up with minions if you don't clear them.

Poltergeist.q: Helen Creech, a spectral woman in a long dress with glowing eyes, roaming her own house.
Poltergeist.j: The odd one out: she has no health and cannot be attacked. You win by finding Carolyn in the item decks and escaping with her.

Inkanyamba.q: A masked man who believes he is a holy avenger and has forgotten his own name. He fights with two daggers.
Inkanyamba.j: 9 health and Horror 4. He raises his own Killer Wrath every phase while it is low, so he gets more dangerous the longer the game lasts.

Terror from Above.q: The game's first vignette, from Series 1. The killer is the birds, a direct homage to the 1963 film.
Terror from Above.j: Short format: it brings Melanie as the Final Girl, and there is no single monster to hit, but a flock.

Evomorph.q: An insectoid alien with a white and red exoskeleton, a scorpion tail and no visible eyes. It was brought on board hidden in the cargo.
Evomorph.j: It evolves by killing. It starts as a slow but crushing hatchling, becomes a fast and fragile youngling, and ends as a slow, strong adult. Its health rises from 4 up to 10.

The Organism.q: Mutated humanoids covered in pustules, in three variants: Fast, Strong and Tough.
The Organism.j: Each variant starts with different health (5, 6 and 7), but all of them start at Horror 5, the highest starting level in Series 2.

The Intruders.q: A trio who believe they are doing holy work by freeing souls: Trish with her axe and skull mask, Baghead with a huge blade, and Zeke, the little one.
The Intruders.j: Horror 3, but 6 health for each of the three. It is not one killer but three bodies covering the board at once.

Big Bad Wolf.q: A gigantic albino werewolf with white fur and glowing red eyes.
Big Bad Wolf.j: 9 health and Horror 5. He has two modes: he starts in Track and switches to Slay when the Dark Power is revealed. Several Terror Cards do different things depending on the mode.

Ratchet Lady.q: A nurse in a torn gown with her head bandaged over the eyes. Her right hand is missing, replaced by a metal frame, and she carries a knife.
Ratchet Lady.j: Horror 5 and 6 health, with no upper health limit. She comes with minions, the Maniacs, and in return you get Calm action cards.

Terror from the Grave.q: Second vignette, from Series 2. The killer is zombies, with Patsy as the Final Girl.
Terror from the Grave.j: A short zombie-genre format: the pressure comes not from one strong enemy but from numbers.

Krampus.q: A bipedal creature with huge horns, grey fur and a reptile tongue. According to the lore he was human before his banishment.
Krampus.j: 10 health and Horror 4. His phase chains a lot: he attacks, picks a target again, moves and leaves a present.

Tormentor.q: The killer of The Marrek Murders, the fourth film in Series 3, set in the Marrek warehouse.
Tormentor.j: Torture horror, with Saw as the clear reference. It brings Mandy and Cassie as Final Girls.

Razorface.q: A demonic humanoid with no lips or nose, his body covered in ritual cuts and hooks chained into his skin.
Razorface.j: 9 health and Horror 5. You start with 3 Affliction cards on him, and to really kill him you have to purge each one by meeting its requirement.

Slayer.q: A bright green figure with a skull head and mossy skin, wrapped in tendrils of blue energy that fill his empty eye sockets.
Slayer.j: 11 health, the biggest health pool in his series, with Horror 4.

Hunter.q: An android hunter. There are actually two: the Mark V, tall and hooded, who disguises himself as a human, and the Mark X, more agile and better built.
Hunter.j: 15 health and Horror 5, but that health only counts for the Mark X. A counter swaps the Mark V for the Mark X near the end.

The Eyeless.q: The killer of Don't Make a Sound, the fifth film in Series 3, set in Utopia.
The Eyeless.j: A monster that hunts by sound, with A Quiet Place and Tremors as references. It brings Meghan and Ronda.

Terror from Destiny.q: Third vignette, from Series 3. The killer is Fate itself, with Gabrielle as the Final Girl.
Terror from Destiny.j: Inspired by Final Destination: there is no body to attack, the danger is the chain of accidents.

Billy.q: A tall, wrecked animatronic bear with no casing on his left arm.
Billy.j: He brings minions that appear during the game and act before him. He also heals 1 every phase while a power source is active, so cutting the power is part of the plan.

Grimlash.q: An ancient god shaped like a bundle of branches and vines, with a glowing pumpkin head and a flaming scythe.
Grimlash.j: 10 health and Horror 4. He hands out Harvest Madness, which gives you extra abilities but ends up killing you. Every victim who dies adds one.

Berith.q: A fallen angel who tempts people into blasphemy and murder. He does not appear on the board himself; Ursula, the nun he possesses, does.
Berith.j: Horror 3 and 7 health, Ursula's. You have to cast him out without killing her, using Divine Blessings to improve her chances of surviving. He does not move in the first part of his phase.

Volk'ar.q: A purple-skinned alien huntress with six yellow eyes along the sides of her face and blades on her forearms. She leaves her prey hanging as trophies.

Raptors.q: The killer of The Raptor Games, the fifth film in Series 4, on Isla Lagarto.
Raptors.j: Dinosaur horror with Jurassic Park as the reference. It brings Maud and Christina.

Terror from Beyond.q: A vignette with no wiki entry of its own yet.

Mort.q: Grey hoodie, red and black trousers and a one-eyed ghost mask. The killer of Shriek, set at a board game convention.
Mort.j: Horror 3 and no health until he is revealed. He starts as one of 10 suspects, all killers from other films: you have to interrogate and pressure five of them to rule them out.

The Happy Trails Horror.mec: No rules of its own. It is the core rulebook and nothing else.
The Happy Trails Horror.com: That is why it is the box to start with: nothing distracts you from learning the game.
The Happy Trails Horror.foro: He is slow and plodding, but he hits extremely hard. Always carry one or two Guards. You can outrun him and loot the far end of the map before he gets there. Don't end your turn on his space: he stabs whoever is next to him for free.

The Haunting of Creech Manor.mec: The Poltergeist has NO health and cannot be damaged. You win by finding Carolyn and getting her out.
The Haunting of Creech Manor.com: The one-way streets make movement even more awkward.
The Haunting of Creech Manor.foro: Weapons are useless here, and so are attack cards. It is the only box where searching for a weapon is wasted time: everything goes into movement, searching and rescuing.

Slaughter in the Groves.mapa: Has its own Divine Wrath track
Slaughter in the Groves.mec: The killer's Wrath track stacks with the map's Divine Wrath. Both act at the same time.
Slaughter in the Groves.com: Consensus: this pairing is brutal. Inkanyamba on another map is far more manageable.
Slaughter in the Groves.foro: The data confirms it: it is the hardest box in the game. If you want to play Inkanyamba without suffering, take him out of Sacred Groves.

Carnage at the Carnival.mapa: Great theme, the traps feel passive
Carnage at the Carnival.mec: 3 puppets as minions. Immortal Master rule: you cannot kill Geppetto while all 3 are in play. Traps on items and on Terror cards.
Carnage at the Carnival.com: It can feel too easy if you clear the puppets early.
Carnage at the Carnival.foro: Be careful searching here: the item traps are nasty. And don't try to finish him off before removing puppets.

Frightmare on Maple Lane.mapa: Dead ends, the Convince action is a chore
Frightmare on Maple Lane.mec: Dream world and Boiler Room. You need the Convince card to enter occupied houses.
Frightmare on Maple Lane.com: Split opinions. It is often called the mechanically weakest box of Series 1, but it has its defenders.

Into the Void.mec: Evolves in 3 stages (Hatchling → Youngling → Adult). It hides after the first victim and attacks from ambush.
Into the Void.com: One of the most versatile for mixing, because its mechanic works on any map. The rules are easy once they click.
Into the Void.foro: It has alternative wins besides killing it: self-destruct the ship and escape, or blow it out an airlock. If the fight turns against you, change goals.

Panic at Station 2891.mapa: Helicopter rescue instead of exits, freezing mechanic
Panic at Station 2891.mec: Victims get tested for infection. Infected ones turn into independent killers.
Panic at Station 2891.com: It is accused of heavy upkeep; others say the two extra systems run smoothly once understood.
Panic at Station 2891.foro: Forum strategy: test the two exposed victims closest to the lab as soon as you can and let the third mutate on its own. Keeping one organism alive at low health gives you the adrenaline die and avoids the "if there is no organism" effects. The axe is ideal because they have low health. And you can send victims to the helicopter by radio without being there yourself.

A Knock at the Door.mapa: The best multi-killer format, with crafting
A Knock at the Door.mec: 3 killers at once, one of them always the "active" one, and it keeps changing. Its own weapon crafting system.
A Knock at the Door.com: Despite the three killers, it is surprisingly easy to follow. It never overwhelms.

Once Upon a Full Moon.mec: Two killer modes, Track and Slay, with different actions. The smallest board of any box.
Once Upon a Full Moon.com: A good second killer after Hans: the two modes create a natural step up in difficulty.
Once Upon a Full Moon.foro: Watch out for one thing: he has a Dark Power that cancels damage from Retaliate and any reaction that hits back. It still blocks the attack, but you do nothing to him. If it shows up, change the plan.

Madness in the Dark.mapa: Pill system and Amped cards, "Final Girl 2.0" card
Madness in the Dark.mec: She heals with no cap as long as you don't attack her. Amped cards (upgraded actions) through the pill system.
Madness in the Dark.com: Described as unpredictable: it depends hugely on how early you take her on.
Madness in the Dark.foro: She doesn't chase you herself; she sends Maniacs who come only for you, relentlessly. And careful: Maniacs cause direct health loss, which can NOT be blocked with Guard or Retaliate. Defensive cards do little here. Go for mobility, rescue fast and always keep an attack in hand.

The Killer from Tomorrow.mapa: The Savior mechanic is very luck-dependent
The Killer from Tomorrow.mec: Two stages (Mark V → Mark X) with different stats. Damage strips off cybernetic parts before he changes stage. There is a VIP victim, the Savior, who must be protected.
The Killer from Tomorrow.com: Frustrating on its own map because rescuing the Savior depends heavily on the dice. Better on other maps. It is also among the most rules-heavy killers in the game.

Hell to Pay.mapa: Modular tiles, the best way into Series 3
Hell to Pay.mec: Afflictions work as optional objectives on top of the normal win condition.
Hell to Pay.com: A community favourite as a Series 3 starting point: demanding without being overwhelming.

The Falconwood Files.mapa: Missions and a mirror dimension, lots of replayability
The Falconwood Files.mec: There is a hidden mirror dimension, a parallel version of every space. A mission system with rewards to choose from.
The Falconwood Files.com: Highly rated for replayability: the choice of missions makes every game play out differently.

The Marrek Murders.mec: The Tormentor does not appear on the board until the Finale. Before that there are only death traps to disarm.
The Marrek Murders.com: The community does not find disarming traps before the Finale very rewarding.

Don't Make a Sound.mapa: The sandworms act as a second killer
Don't Make a Sound.mec: Noise mechanic: your own actions make noise, which draws the killer in and activates it.
Don't Make a Sound.com: An interesting concept, but the community feels it is not taken all the way.

Bad Times at Buddyland.mapa: 4 arcade spaces as a hot spot
Bad Times at Buddyland.mec: The Buddies are minions with their own health, initiative and attack. You cannot attack Billy while a Buddy is on his space. He heals on the heart symbol while 1 of the 4 power sources stays active, and you can shut those down by spending time. The epic Finale brings out a second killer, Boris: you have to kill both.
Bad Times at Buddyland.com: Nicknamed "the Camp Happy Trails of Series 4": a good testing ground.

A Rotten Harvest.mapa: The children act as independent enemies
A Rotten Harvest.mec: Harvest Madness track: a heart either heals OR lowers madness, never both. Levels 1-3 give a bonus of your choice. Going past level 3 is an instant loss. The children kidnap victims to take them to the altar.
A Rotten Harvest.com: The risk-reward tension of that track is highly rated.

A Demon in the Shadows.mapa: Malice and the blessed/cursed dice system
A Demon in the Shadows.mec: A two-part win: defeat the possessed nun Ursula and then revive her with Divine Blessings. Malice spaces swap your die for the cursed one. Placing all 14 Malice tokens is an instant loss.
A Demon in the Shadows.com: The most atmospheric killer of Series 4, and the map is among the best in the game.

The Green Terror.mec: Hidden movement with a deck of route cards. Hidden/Visible states with different actions. A successful attack reveals his route; a missed one triggers the ambush penalty.
The Green Terror.com: The only hidden-movement killer in the game, very tense. But the community warns: hidden movement adds to an already complex loop, and the board is hard to read. One of the most rules-demanding.

The Raptor Games.mec: The pack's health is the number of raptors, with no cap. Loose raptors stop on victims instead of attacking them. The T-Rex cannot be killed, moves 2 per round and eats in a fixed order: victims, raptors, Final Girl, killer. Three electric fences block movement and line of sight; a die roll in Upkeep decides which are active. Rescuing costs 1 extra time.
The Raptor Games.com: Preliminary data: the box is very recent and there is little experience with it.

The North Pole Nightmare.mapa: A village with the Christmas tree in the middle
The North Pole Nightmare.mec: Present system: the elves (the victims) reveal presents with a random good or bad effect, and you can risk opening them. It brings its own vehicle, the reindeer.
The North Pole Nightmare.com: Along with Shriek, the only box that comes with miniatures. Krampus starts with 10 health and Horror 4, according to a community source.

Shriek.mec: Mort does not start on the board: he is hidden among 10 randomly placed suspects. Interrogate and Coerce cards reveal clues that eliminate suspects until one is left. Until he is unmasked, certain Terror cards let a random suspect act as the killer. Victims don't panic until he is unmasked.
Shriek.com: A tongue-in-cheek homage to Scream. It is the most recent release, and there is little experience with it yet.

rev.Madness in the Dark: Highly rated for design, and one of the hardest in the game. Three reviews agree: the asylum and the pills are loved, Ratchet Lady frustrates. Not a box to start with.
